headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading-error when Goose ingests Perplexity outputs; shared filesystem and broad egress also create medium data-leakage and capability-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while Perplexity produces web-derived browsing context and citations. If Goose ingests Perplexity output as trusted text, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use. This is not proven by a shared channel, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Goose is configured to consume Perplexity answers as instructions or prompts
IF Perplexity output is copied into a Goose task without sanitization
mitigations: Paste Perplexity output into a plain-text buffer first and remove imperative language
Add a fixed system prompt that forbids following instructions from retrieved content
Require human review before Goose executes any MCP or shell action
Use a delimiter/template that separates evidence from instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress; Perplexity uploads documents and browsing context to vendor-hosted services. A shared workspace or copied files can move sensitive code or documents into Perplexity’s backend, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or proprietary source code
IF files from Goose are uploaded into Perplexity for analysis
mitigations: Exclude secrets and .env files from the shared workspace
Upload only redacted excerpts to Perplexity
Move sensitive repos into a separate directory not used with Perplexity
Turn off automatic file attachment in the workflow
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or file-classification gates before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state; Perplexity cannot write locally, but it can still influence shared work products through browser-based outputs. The main conflict is on shared files and git-adjacent artifacts in the same workspace, which can cause overwrites or inconsistent edits even without direct write access from Perplexity.
conditions: IF Goose and Perplexity are used on the same working directory
IF Perplexity-generated text is manually merged into files that Goose also edits
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Review git diffs before each commit
Avoid concurrent sessions on the same repo
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking and merge arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity’s output is often treated as an answer engine result, and Goose can act on text via shell, filesystem, and MCP. If Goose accepts Perplexity’s claims without verification, a mistaken or hallucinated answer can cascade into code changes or operational actions. That blast radius is larger than a single document, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Goose uses Perplexity output as authoritative input
IF Goose is allowed to execute shell or MCP actions based on that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Limit Goose to drafting changes, not applying them
Ask Perplexity for citations and inspect them manually
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles source code and local files, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context on vendor-hosted infrastructure. If regulated or confidential data is moved from Goose into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated data from Goose is uploaded to Perplexity
IF the organization requires local-only retention for the same data class
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity
Use anonymized or synthetic samples
Check the vendor privacy policy before sharing documents
Keep compliance-sensitive work in Goose only
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and retention review
